big_picture_notes: Zechariah divides into two distinct halves. Chapters 1–8 are dated encouragement oracles centered on a cycle of eight night visions (chs. 1–6), capped by a crowning sign‑act and followed by prose oracles on fasting and future blessing (chs. 7–8). Chapters 9–14 shift to undated, apocalyptic 'burdens' (maśśāʾ) marked by oracle formulas (9:1; 12:1), focusing on judgment/salvation, the humble king, shepherd imagery, repentance/cleansing, and the climactic Day of Yahweh. Literary glue: dating formulas, the interpreting angel motif, repeated 'Thus says Yahweh of hosts,' and the burden/oracle markers framing the second half.

stories.story_title: The Eight Night Visions and the Temple's Hope
stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: A dated sequence beginning with introductory repentance (1:1–6) and night visions (from 1:7) through the crowning sign‑act (6:9–15). Start (1:1): first date/oracle establishes context. End (6:15): conditional promise that the temple will be built by those from afar—vision cycle resolved. Glue: 'I lifted up my eyes and saw' vision markers, the interpreting angel refrain, restoration/cleansing themes.

scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Dated oracle recalls fathers’ disobedience and justice fulfilled; closes with acknowledgment that Yahweh’s words overtook them. Devices: exhortation, retrospective validation.

scenes.scene_name: The Horsemen Among the Myrtle Trees
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The first night-vision: patrol-riders reporting all the earth at rest while Jerusalem still lies desolate.
The angel's intercession over the seventy years, answered by God's jealous love for Zion.

scenes.scene_name: I Will Return to Jerusalem with Mercy
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Anger at the complacent nations and the promise that His house and a measuring line will be restored.

scenes.scene_name: Vision of the Four Horns and Four Smiths
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Horns that scattered Judah; smiths sent to terrify and cast them down. Devices: symbolic agents, terse Q&A interpretation.

scenes.scene_name: A Wall of Fire Around Her
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The man with the measuring line; Jerusalem a city without walls, with God Himself as a wall of fire and glory.
The summons to flee Babylon, for whoever touches God's people touches the apple of His eye.

scenes.scene_name: Many Nations Will Join the LORD
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The call to rejoice as God comes to dwell, many nations joined to Him — 'be silent before the LORD.'
The high priest in filthy garments, Satan at his right hand, rebuked by the LORD.
The filthy clothes exchanged for splendid robes and a clean turban, with the charge to walk in God's ways.
The messianic sign: the Branch, the seven-eyed stone, and iniquity removed in a single day.

scenes.scene_name: The Gold Lampstand and Two Olive Trees
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The vision of the seven-lamped lampstand flanked by two olive trees.

scenes.scene_name: Not by Might, but by My Spirit
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The word to Zerubbabel: the great mountain leveled to a plain, the capstone brought with shouts of grace.
Zerubbabel's hands to finish the temple — 'who has despised the day of small things?'
The two olive branches explained: the anointed ones who stand by the Lord of all the earth.
Cursing scroll flies over land to consume houses of thieves and perjurers. Devices: written curse as active agent; covenant sanctions.
The measuring basket of the land's iniquity, with Wickedness personified as a woman shoved inside.

scenes.scene_name: Carried to the Land of Shinar
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The stork-winged women lifting the basket away to build it a house in Babylon.
The final vision: four chariots with colored horses coming from between two bronze mountains.
The four spirits going out to patrol the earth, giving rest to God's Spirit in the north.
The crowning of Joshua as a sign of the Branch who will build the temple of the LORD.
The royal-priestly Branch ruling in peace, the crown a memorial, the far-off coming to build.

stories.story_title: The Question of Fasting and the Future of Zion
stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: A dated prose unit responding to fasting inquiry: indicts past self‑serving ritual (7) and promises restoration/ethics and feast‑reversal (8). Start (7:1): fourth‑year date. End (8:23): nations grasp a Jew’s robe—God is with you. Glue: inclusio around fasting (7:3; 8:18–19) and repeated 'Thus says Yahweh of hosts.'

scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The delegation's question about continuing the fasts of mourning over the temple's fall.
God's probing answer: their fasting and feasting were for themselves, not for Him.
The recurring prophetic word: show devotion, and do not oppress the widow, orphan, foreigner, or poor.
The fathers' stubborn refusal that brought God's anger and the scattering whirlwind.

scenes.scene_name: Old Men and Children in the Streets
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: God's jealous return to dwell in the City of Truth, its streets full of the aged and playing children.
What seems impossible to the remnant is not impossible to God, who will gather His people home.
'Let your hands be strong'; reversal from no wage/peace to fruitful vine/peaceful conditions. Devices: contrastive parallelism, builder exhortation.

scenes.scene_name: Ethical Mandates for the Restored Community
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: From purposed disaster to purposed good; speak truth, judge peace; Yahweh hates falsehood. Devices: purpose chiasm, concise ethics.
Fasts of months become joyful feasts; nations seek Yahweh in Jerusalem; ten men grasp a Jew’s robe. Devices: reversal motif, synecdoche for universal pilgrimage.

stories.story_title: The First Burden: Judgment, the Lowly King, and the Worthless Shepherd
stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Undated apocalyptic burden beginning at 9:1; moves from neighbor judgments to humble king (9:9–10), covenant‑victory and restoration, then allegory of shepherd and broken staffs. Start (9:1): burden formula. End (11:17): woe on the worthless shepherd—unit closure. Glue: shepherd/covenant motifs and swift progression from hope to rejection.

scenes.scene_name: The Burden Against Hadrach and Tyre
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The oracle sweeping over Syria and proud, wealthy Tyre, whom the Lord will cast into the sea.

scenes.scene_name: I Will Camp Around My House
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Judgment on the Philistine cities and the promise that no oppressor will again overrun God's people.
'Rejoice greatly' summons; king on a donkey; ends with worldwide peace and dominion. Devices: contrastive royal imagery, messianic proclamation.
The blood of the covenant freeing the prisoners, and Judah drawn as God's bow against Greece.
The LORD appearing as a storm-warrior to save His flock, who will sparkle like jewels over His land.

scenes.scene_name: Call for Rain and Divine Leadership
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Ask Yahweh for rain; reject diviners; cornerstone/tent‑peg/battle‑bow metaphors for leadership. Devices: polemic against false counsel, leadership metaphors.
The strengthening of Judah and Joseph, redeemed and as numerous as before.
The scattered remembering God in distant lands, brought back through the sea of distress.
'Open your doors, O Lebanon' lament; cedars devoured; shepherds wail. Devices: personification, hyperbole, transitional lament.

scenes.scene_name: Pasture the Flock Marked for Slaughter
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The shepherd sign-act begins over a flock sold without remorse, whom God will no longer pity.
The two staffs taken up and the three shepherds dismissed amid mutual loathing.
The staff Favor cut in two, revoking the covenant — recognized as the word of the LORD.
The wages weighed out and thrown to the potter (fulfilled at Christ's betrayal), and Union broken.
The foolish shepherd raised up who devours the flock — 'woe to the worthless shepherd!'

stories.story_title: The Second Burden: Mourning, Cleansing, and Final Battle
stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Second burden (12:1) weaves mourning for the pierced one, cleansing, end of idols/false prophets, striking/refining of shepherded remnant, and the climactic Day of Yahweh with universal holiness. Start (12:1): burden formula. End (14:21): no Canaanite/trader in Yahweh’s house—absolute holiness. Glue: repeated 'on that day' stitching the apocalyptic tapestry.

scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Jerusalem made a cup of drunkenness and a heavy stone that injures all who try to heave it away.
Horses struck with panic and the clans of Judah made a consuming flame among the nations.
God defending Jerusalem so the feeblest become like David, and the house of David like God.

scenes.scene_name: Mourning for the Pierced One and Cleansing
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Spirit poured out; they look on the pierced; deep lament; fountain opened for sin and impurity. Devices: lament genre, repentance‑to‑cleansing arc.

scenes.scene_name: End of Idolatry and False Prophets
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Names of idols cut off; prophets ashamed/deny prophetic identity; wounds explained away. Devices: purification oracle, shame/denial motif.

scenes.scene_name: Striking the Shepherd and Refining the Remnant
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: 'Awake, O sword' against my shepherd; two‑thirds cut; one‑third refined; covenant exchange restored. Devices: shepherd/flock metaphor, refining imagery.
The Day of the LORD: the city captured and half exiled before the LORD goes out to fight.

scenes.scene_name: His Feet on the Mount of Olives
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The Mount of Olives split to form a valley of escape, on a unique day with evening light.

scenes.scene_name: The LORD King Over All the Earth
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Living water flowing from Jerusalem, the LORD reigning alone, the city dwelling secure forever.
The rotting plague and great panic on those who warred against Jerusalem, with their wealth collected.
Survivors keep Feast of Booths; bells and pots 'Holy to Yahweh'; no Canaanite in Yahweh’s house. Devices: cultic imagery, holiness inclusio, universal worship.
